summary: This BCP specifies the approval process for changes to the IANA "IPv6 Address Space" registry and updates RFC 7249.

eli5.summary: The big map of IPv6 address blocks needs rules for who can change it. This sets the approval steps.

questions: who approves ipv6 address space registry changes
what is the approval process for ipv6 allocations
subtitle: Require stricter approval for major changes to the IPv6 address space registry.

tldr.problem: The IPv6 Address Space registry had weak "IESG approval" as its allocation policy for non-routine changes, which is insufficient for decisions about the vast majority of the spare address space.
tldr.mechanism: This BCP changes the approval policy from "IESG approval" to "IETF Review", requiring more thorough community consensus for major address allocations.
tldr.outcome: Future large IPv6 address space changes must follow the stricter IETF Review process, ensuring broader oversight.

today: RFC 9812 is a Best Current Practice document that updates RFC 7249. It remains the current policy for IPv6 address space allocation decisions.

sections.title: The IPv6 Address Space and Its Management
sections.content: The IPv6 address space is enormous, with the bulk of it reserved by the IETF for future global unicast address assignments. The management of IPv6 address allocations was delegated to IANA by RFC 1881. Occasionally, address space allocations are performed outside the scope of routine regional registry assignments, such as when moving address ranges between different IANA registries. For example, RFC 9602 requested a substantial allocation moving the range 5f00::/16 from the main IPv6 Address Space registry to the IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Space registry.
sections.eli5: The internet has a big map of IPv6 addresses that are set aside for future use. Sometimes someone wants to change which part of the map is used for what, and the internet needs to decide if that is okay.

sections.title: Strengthening the Approval Policy
sections.content: RFC 7249 documented the allocation policy for IPv6 address space allocations reserved by the IETF, which was listed as "IESG approval". However, this policy is defined in RFC 8126 as a weak requirement: the IESG has discretion to request documentation but is not required to, and it is described as a fallback mechanism for cases where other approval processes cannot be used. This weak standard is inappropriate for decisions affecting the majority of the spare IPv6 address space. This document changes the approval policy to "IETF Review" as defined in RFC 8126, which requires broader community participation and approval through the standards process. This ensures that major address space allocations receive the careful deliberation they deserve.
sections.eli5: The old rule only needed a small group to agree, but for something this important, it is better to have everyone in the community review and agree that the change is a good idea.

sections.title: Status Clarification
sections.content: This document also clarifies the status of RFC 1881, which defined the initial IPv6 address allocation management policy. RFC 1881 was a joint publication of the IAB and IESG following an IETF Last Call, making it part of the IETF Stream. However, it was incorrectly listed as "Legacy" in the RFC index at the time of writing. This clarification ensures that RFC 1881 is properly recognized as an IETF document, not a legacy reference.
sections.eli5: An old paper that set up the system was mislabeled as old history, when it is actually still important. This fixes the label so people know it is part of the official rules.
